source: Bunker tests at INSEMEX Petrosani on two beam-column specimens (CODEC project's specimens; FRAMEBLAST project), from the test paper: F. Dinu, I. Marginean, D. Dubina, A. Kovacs and E. Ghicioi, Experimental testing and numerical modeling of steel frames under close-in detonations, Procedia Engineering 210 (2017) 377-385, doi:10.1016/j.proeng.2017.11.091 (sections 2-3, Table 1, Figs. 1-6; obtained 30 October 2026). The full-scale building's shots are from FRAMEBLAST's technical report, stage II, 2018 (Politehnica University Timisoara), pp. 7-10, via the Internet Archive.
licence: Numbers transcribed or read off figures (facts); the sources are not redistributed. Procedia Engineering 210 is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (stated in the PDF's metadata); the FRAMEBLAST report states no licence.

specimen.column: HEB260, flanges reduced to 160 mm wide, weak axis in the frame's plane (section 2)
specimen.lengthNote: between the column's end plates, Fig. 2; the drawing places the beams' bottom flange about 1.27 m above the column's bottom, where the text puts the charge at 1.25 m and 0.30 m below that flange
specimen.supports: pin-type supports at both ends (Fig. 1b), the top fixed to the bunker's roof (Fig. 1a); the paper's model pins the column bases
specimen.beams: two half-span IPE220 (1.40 m each, Fig. 2) on extended end plates 370 x 160 x 16 mm with M16 10.9 bolts to the flanges; one half-span transverse IPE220 on an L100x50x10 cleat to the web, its far end on the bunker's wall; tubular lateral restraints at the longitudinal beams' ends

steelNote: S275 J0, Table 1: average measured values; Agt is the total elongation at the maximum force. The elongation after fracture and the tensile specimens' gauge length are not given.

charge.explosive: TNT equivalence 1 (section 3); the explosive is not named
charge.shape: assembled from cylindrical units of 0.121 kg (Fig. 3a); the units' size and the assembly are not given
charge.heightNote: above the column's base, and 0.30 m below the beams' bottom flange
charge.mounting: hung freely from the bunker's ceiling, facing the web (Fig. 1b)
charge.standoffNote: measured from the column web's face

gauges.strain: S1-S8 on the column's web, specimen 2 only, in pairs at 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 m below the beams' bottom flange and 80 mm from the web's centreline (Fig. 2); the bottom pair is 0.565 m above the column's bottom; S6 is in the pair 0.5 m below the beams
gauges.pressure: two sensors 3.5 m from the specimen, in front of the bunker's venting (Fig. 1c)

shots.name: m4
shots.dishNote: permanent out-of-plane deformation of the web, 'approximately'; no visible cracks; the paper ascribes the difference to the charge's orientation
shots.gaugeNote: specimen 2, Figs. 4d and 5; the peak within the first millisecond

shots.name: m5
shots.breachNote: 'almost' 600 and 500 mm: the web completely removed around the point of detonation, the fracture lines along the fillets; in the photographs (Fig. 3b-c) the hole spans the web between the fillets and its top is at the beams' connection

bunkerFit.note: peak overpressure P = A (R / W^b)^a in kPa fitted to the sensors' peaks (section 3)

fullScaleBuilding.source: FRAMEBLAST technical report, stage II, 2018, pp. 7-10: a 2 x 2 bay, two-storey frame of HEB260 columns at Petrosani, floors loaded to 10 kN/m2 by water tanks, charges 1.8 m above ground (1.5 m above the foundation) near the central ground-floor column, cumulative on the same column

shots.name: E3
shots.outcome: first permanent deformation: web at the charge and the flanges

shots.name: E5
shots.outcome: web dished; the flanges act partly as a reflector

shots.name: E8
shots.outcome: column removed; adjacent beams left with permanent deflection

fullScaleBuilding.explosiveNote: explosive type not stated; below 560 g no plastic deformation
